title: Abstract Classes and Methods
learning_outcomes: Explain what abstract classes and methods contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: abstract classes.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Object-oriented code groups state and behavior. Classes should protect their invariants, expose a clear public API, and use inheritance only when the subtype relationship is meaningful. In this lesson, focus on abstract classes; then compare it with abstract methods. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use abstract classes and methods when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Object-oriented code groups state and behavior. Classes should protect their invariants, expose a clear public API, and use inheritance only when the subtype relationship is meaningful. For abstract classes and methods, begin with abstract classes. Also distinguish abstract methods; shared implementation; required subclass behavior. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

content_blocks.title: A small PHP example for Abstract Classes and Methods
content_blocks.code:
<?php
interface Describable { public function describe(): string; }
final class Product implements Describable { public function describe(): string { return "Product ready"; } }
echo (new Product())->describe() . PHP_EOL;

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
